newsitem.title: USA: USDA to buy Fla. orange juice to aid producers.
newsitem.headline: USDA to buy Fla. orange juice to aid producers.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said it would buy Florida orange juice to help citrus producers in that state whose crops were devastated by the recent freeze.
USDA said it will purchase 342,720 cases of canned orange juice and 192,000 cases of single strength orange juice.
"Florida citrus growers are suffering what may turn out to be one of the worst crop losses in seven years," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement.
"The department is making this purchase to help alleviate the economic impact caused by the winter freeze," he said.
USDA said it will donate the orange juice to the Child Nutrition Program and other domestic food assistance programs.
USDA said the purchase will be made by its Agricultural Marketing Service from offers that must be submitted on a delivered-to-destination basis.

USDA said offers for canned orange juice were due Feb. 18, acceptance was set for March 4 and the delivery period was April 1 - August 31. It said it was seeking cases consisting of 12 46 ounce containers.

The department said offers for single strength orange juice were due March 12, with acceptance set for March 24 and a delivery period of April 16 - June 30. USDA said it seeks cases made up of 70 four ounce cartons.
USDA said the quantities may be subject to change depending upon prices, quantities offered, and possible adjustments in user requirements.

It said details and specifications will be mailed soon to vendors. Offers to sell must be received by the Commodity Procurement Branch, Fruit and Vegetable Division, Agricultural Marketing Service, P.O. Box 23693, Washington, D.C. 20026-3693, not later than 1 p.m. ET on the date due, USDA said.
